applicable_when: The B matrix has layout stride_bk=1, stride_bn=192 (column-major: B[k,n] stored at offset k + 192*n). The current load computes xindex = idx_n + 96*idx_m with a double-broadcast of idx_m + 192*idx_n — this mixes two different index expressions (wrong stride 96 vs correct 192, wrong dimension ordering) and produces a non-contiguous access pattern across the BLOCK_N dimension. When Triton stages these loads through shared memory, consecutive threads access addresses 192 elements apart, causing 7.9-way bank conflicts. The fix is to load B as a [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] tile with the correct column-major stride (k*1 + n*192), then pass it directly to tl.dot. Additionally, reducing BLOCK_N from 128 to 64 (since N=96 means BLOCK_N=128 wastes 25% of compute and inflates register usage) and reducing BLOCK_M from 64 to 32 will cut register pressure, allowing more blocks/SM and improving occupancy. Previous correctness failures (max_diff ~70) were caused by incorrect index remapping in the B load — this plan fixes the index expression directly without TMA or other structural changes.
